candidates.rationale: The floor and ceiling share one 21-day window somewhat arbitrarily; making the ceiling a fast 5-day recent high while keeping a stable 21-day floor tests whether proximity to a quickly-decaying resistance level, not a symmetric channel, carries the signal. A single literal edit on this island's best-performing, already near-optimal parent.

Static E/P treats a shrinking-earnings cheap stock the same as a growing one; per rule 12's validated delta/spread shape, wrapping the level in a 63-day change (fundamental deltas need this width for coverage) turns pure value into value-plus-earnings-momentum without touching the close denominator rule 10 already flagged as collinear across OHLC fields.

The raw $dollar_volume denominator mixes cross-sectional liquidity scale into what should be a stock-relative ratio; af43733e3a6a1dbf already validated recasting it as TS_RANK($dollar_volume,5) for this exact close-low/dollar_volume family (fitness 7.646 to 11.707), so this retests the same fix at a longer 21-day liquidity-rank horizon, distinct from that window.

Rule 11 shows the DELAY($close,1) overnight-gap ratio is the validated core (the DELAY($open,1) sibling failed cheap_screen), leaving the 10-day smoothing horizon as the only untested free choice; lengthening it to 21 tests whether the gap-persistence signal holds over a monthly window.

Rule 6 names this exact TS_MEAN($dollar_volume/$open,W) ratio chassis saturated and says stop touching its numerator/denominator field or window, leaving the root combinator as the only legal lever; summing rather than differencing the two rank legs tests whether they reinforce a shared 'wide range relative to a normalizer' signal instead of cancelling it.

TS_SUM($return,63) is the same return-sum pattern id49's own lesson flagged as this run's dominant failure mode (rule 11); id49 already fixed it via a dollar-volume delta from this same parent, so this swaps the flagged leg for a plain liquidity-level rank instead, a distinct fix to the same weak component.

A bare RANK($roa) has no conditioning at all; id50 already tried pairing it with dollar_volume (fitness only 1.393) and id62 already swapped the field to accrual_gap outright, so this instead pairs roa with accrual_gap directly (profitable AND low-accrual), a genuine quality-composite interaction neither prior mutation captures.

This CS_RANK(fundamental)*TS_RANK(dollar_volume,W) template is already the validated shape; the 63-day liquidity-rank window is its only untested free parameter, so shortening it to 21 tests a faster liquidity-ranking horizon for the same quality x attention interaction.

This exact parent already spawned three single-slot mutations (id44 smoothed leg1, id64 ranked leg2, id51 shortened the window to 5), and swapping volume for dollar_volume here is known to collapse to rho 0.994; the untested slow window (63) is the one remaining safe lever.

Same raw-dollar_volume-denominator weakness as its close-low sibling, which af43733e3a6a1dbf already fixed via TS_RANK($dollar_volume,5); applying the same fix here at window 10 (distinct from that sibling's 5 and from this batch's own close-low mutation at 21) avoids reproducing either one's denominator subtree.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.


TASK: MUTATE. For each parent below, identify its single weakest component and
change ONLY that component.

A mutation is localized: the returned expression must be within
3 tree edits of its parent. Rewriting the idea is not a mutation
and will be rejected. Say which node you changed in `changed_node`, and put the
parent's id in `parent_ids`.

Each parent is shown with its fitness and nothing else. Fitness is a single scalar in which higher is better; it already accounts for significance, year-to-year stability, complexity and turnover. You are not given per-year, coverage, turnover or horizon diagnostics in this run, so choose the component to change from the expression itself.

Working memory: rules written after earlier rounds on this island, oldest first. Apply them.
  1. Leverage-based factors failed the cheap screen twice this round (delta of leverage over 63 days at t=0.62, leverage zscore times return volatility at t=0.45). Leverage alone is weak signal in the 2000-2013 cheap window here; it needs a stronger co-factor or should be deprioritized for now.
  2. For roe, level-vs-trend framing is weak (roe minus its 63-day EMA failed cheap screen at t=0.38) while change-volatility framing is strong (volatility of daily roe changes was accepted at fitness 2.184). Prefer second-moment/volatility constructions over deviation-from-trend for this field.
  3. Bare intraday range ratios normalized by a rolling min or max keep falling just short of the cheap screen even at their best this round (high-low over low-minus-rolling-min at t=0.71, high-minus-rolling-max times a volume-delta zscore at t=0.91). This family needs a stronger secondary signal than a bare range ratio to clear the bar.
  4. Two rejects this round were exact duplicates of earlier proposals in the same run (a 63-day roa delta, and a 21-day correlation of absolute return with volume). Check new candidates against this round's own proposal list, not just the archive, before submitting.
  5. A price/range/return leg multiplied by TS_RANK($dollar_volume, W) fails cheap_screen even though the same pair can pass as a TS_CORR: CS_RANK($high-$low)*TS_RANK($dollar_volume,63) scored t=0.43 and TS_SUM($return,40)*TS_RANK($dollar_volume,63) scored t=0.85, while CS_RANK(fundamental)*TS_RANK(volume/price stat) again cleared everything (fitness 1.864). Reserve the multiply-combinator for a fundamental leg; use TS_CORR for price/range-vs-volume pairs.
  6. CS_RANK(($high-$low)/(TS_MAX($high,21)+eps)) and its TS_MEAN($dollar_volume or $open, W) sibling are a saturated chassis: 3 of this round's rejects swapped only the numerator or the denominator's field/window and still shared 5-10 nodes with an archive member. Stop generating new candidates on this exact ratio shape.
  7. Two-leg RANK(A) op RANK(B) proposals still collide on archive_subtree when only one leg changes and the other is left byte-identical to an archived leg (RANK($roa)-RANK(TS_SUM($return,63)); RANK(TS_DELTA($operating_margin,63))*RANK($asset_turnover)). Mutate both legs together, not just one.
  8. Bare TS_RANK of a raw fundamental level fails at any window, for different gates: TS_RANK($roa,63) missed cheap_screen (t=0.86), TS_RANK($roe,252) missed coverage (0.871). Apply TS_DELTA to a fundamental before ranking or smoothing it, as the accepted TS_STD(TS_DELTA(field,1),W) pair did.
  9. A single-fundamental TS_STD-normalized momentum spread narrowly missed cheap_screen (t=0.89) while a CS_ZSCORE of a spread between two different fundamentals at matched windows scored 3.081 — worth retesting, since cross-field, CS_ZSCORE, and matched windows all changed at once so the cause isn't isolated yet.
  10. Swapping the OHLC field used as a ratio's denominator doesn't decorrelate a fundamental-ratio factor: $eps/$open vs $eps/$close hit rho 0.825. Treat OHLC fields as collinear, the same way the already-flagged smoothing-operator and volume-normalizer swaps are.
  11. A smoothed price_t/price_(t-1) ratio fails cheap_screen the same way $return-driven kernels do (TS_MEAN($open/DELAY($open,1),10) scored t=0.32) — screen out manually reconstructed 'synthetic returns' too, not just proposals that reference $return directly.
  12. This round's fundamental accepts all wrapped roe/roa/accrual_gap in a delta or a between-field spread rather than ranking a level directly; keep building on that shape rather than plain fundamental-level transforms.

Return exactly one mutation per parent, 10 in total.
